title: Tampered and Fraudulent Document Detection
summary: Score claim documents for signs of editing, fabrication and reuse, explain each signal, and route high-risk files to your investigation team instead of labelling anyone a fraudster.

seo.title: Tampered Claim Document Detection with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that checks claim bills, reports and repair invoices for editing, fabrication and reuse, explains each signal and routes risky files to investigators.

problem.intro: Reimbursement bills, motor repair invoices and death-claim papers are easy to alter with free editing tools. A changed amount on a pharmacy bill, a back-dated discharge summary or one hospital bill reused across several claims rarely stands out to an assessor working through a queue.

pain_points.title: Edits are invisible at a glance
pain_points.detail: A retyped amount or date on a scanned bill looks normal on screen, and forensic checks are too slow to run by hand on every file.

pain_points.title: Fabricated documents from templates
pain_points.detail: Bills generated from online templates can carry real hospital names, plausible GSTINs and registration numbers that only fail on closer checking.

pain_points.title: Reuse across claims and channels
pain_points.detail: The same bill, prescription or photograph can appear in claims under different policies or from different agents, and nobody sees both files side by side.

pain_points.title: Investigators get weak referrals
pain_points.detail: Referrals based on gut feel waste investigation capacity and create unfair friction for genuine customers.

solution.overview: We build a document forensics layer that runs on every claim document as it is submitted. It examines the file, the image and the content: PDF structure and metadata, signs of local editing or pasted regions in images, arithmetic and date logic, and identifiers such as GSTIN or registration numbers against reference data you hold. It also searches your claim archive for near-duplicate pages. Each document gets a risk score with the specific signals that triggered it and highlighted regions on the page. High-risk files go to your fraud control unit as a case pack; everything else continues through normal processing, with a sample kept for quality review.
capabilities: Checks PDF structure and metadata for incremental edits, unusual producer software and font substitutions
Detects pasted, cloned or locally altered regions in scanned and photographed images
Recalculates bill totals, taxes and line items and checks date sequences across documents
Validates GSTIN format and check digit, and hospital and doctor registration numbers against reference data
Finds near-duplicate pages and photographs across your historical claim archive
Produces an explained risk score with page overlays and a case pack for investigators

workflow.title: Collect original files
workflow.detail: Documents are taken as originally submitted, before any compression or re-scanning, together with claim metadata.

workflow.title: Run file and image forensics
workflow.detail: PDF structure, metadata and image-level checks look for signs of editing, splicing or generation from templates.

workflow.title: Check content logic
workflow.detail: Arithmetic, dates, identifiers and cross-document consistency are tested against rules and reference data.

workflow.title: Search for reuse
workflow.detail: Perceptual hashes and text fingerprints are compared with the claim archive to find repeated pages or photos.

workflow.title: Score and route
workflow.detail: Signals combine into an explained risk score; files above the threshold go to the fraud control unit as a case pack.

workflow.title: Investigate and feed back
workflow.detail: Investigators record outcomes, which are used to tune thresholds and retire noisy signals.

inputs: Claim documents as originally submitted: native PDFs, scans and photos
Claim metadata: policy, claimant, provider, amounts and dates
Historical claim document archive for reuse search
Provider master and reference data for GSTIN and registration checks
Past investigation outcomes, where available, for calibration
outputs: Document-level risk score with the list of triggered signals
Page overlays highlighting suspected edited or pasted regions
Near-duplicate matches with links to the earlier claims
Investigator case pack ready for the fraud control unit
Signal performance log based on investigation outcomes
human_in_the_loop: Investigators in your fraud control unit review every high-risk referral and decide whether to investigate, query or clear the claim. The system surfaces signals only; it never rejects a claim or labels a customer, hospital or garage as fraudulent.
integrations: Core claims or TPA platform (via API or document export)
Document management system or claim archive storage
Fraud control unit case management tool
guardrails: Signals explained in plain language; no unexplained scores reach investigators
Thresholds set and reviewed with the fraud control unit, with periodic checks for skew against particular regions or provider types
Re-photographed or heavily compressed documents marked as low forensic value rather than scored as suspicious
No automatic claim rejection or customer communication
Original files preserved unaltered for evidential use
compliance_notes: Supports the fraud monitoring framework and investigation function that IRDAI expects insurers to maintain, without replacing investigator judgement.
Claim archives are searched only for fraud prevention and claim handling, consistent with purpose limitation under the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: A retrospective run on historical reimbursement claims for one line of business, including files your investigators have already confirmed as tampered and a larger set of cleared claims.
deliverables: Signal catalogue agreed with the fraud control unit
Forensics pipeline run on the historical sample
Investigator review screen with page overlays
Recommendation on thresholds and production roll-out

what_we_measure.how: Share of high-risk referrals that investigators agree merit further investigation.
How many previously confirmed tampered files the pipeline flags in the retrospective run.
Number of cleared claims flagged, reviewed by investigators to see which signals caused them.
Timed on case packs compared with the current referral format.

faqs.q: Will customers be accused on the basis of an AI score?
faqs.a: No. A score is a reason to look closer, not a finding. Investigators decide what happens next, and the case pack shows exactly which signals fired so their reasoning can be checked.

faqs.q: Does it work on photographs of documents?
faqs.a: Partly. Content, arithmetic and reuse checks work on photos, but pixel-level forensics are weaker once a document has been printed and re-photographed. The system marks such files as low forensic value instead of treating them as suspicious.

faqs.q: Can it check documents against other insurers' claims?
faqs.a: Only against data you hold or are entitled to use. If you take part in an industry data-sharing arrangement, we can design an interface to it, but we do not assume access.

faqs.q: How do you avoid unfair targeting of certain hospitals or regions?
faqs.a: Thresholds and signal performance are reviewed by provider type and region during the pilot, and noisy signals are dropped. Investigators see the evidence behind each flag, not a list of whom to suspect.
